whatWorks: Identity across the three states holds cleanly: 5003 is still 5003 in stress and recovery, the figure keeps its primitive family and its charcoal/ochre pairing, and recovery returns close to neutral. The identityAnchors requirement is already satisfied and must not be traded away when fracture is added.

Each token has exactly one dominant figure and no competing second subject. There is no even field of incident and no scattered all-over composition, so the singular focal hierarchy the brief asks for is structurally present even though the figure is the wrong size and weight.

The ground is genuinely near-black and the secondary members sit at a very low value against it, so the two-tier value structure (bright accent over dark iron over near-black) already exists as a mechanism. The hue pair itself, ochre against cold charcoal, is the correct pair.

The 5265/5920/6444 triangle and the 5789 diamond prove the runtime can produce a broad, edge-reaching outer contour rather than only rosettes, so the silhouette vocabulary is not locked to concentric rings.

findings.whatFails: Every token in all four sheets is drawn as thin open stroke with a completely empty near-black interior, and the recursive child generations are tiny grey specks that sit outside or straddle the ochre outline (5134, 5396, 6051, 6444) rather than nesting inside it. Nothing anywhere in the sheet is a filled area.
findings.why: The brief's subject is weight, and the direction says the form must be 'solid where it exists' and that inner generations are 'few and large so they read as part of the same silhouette'. An outline has no mass by construction: it is a diagram of a shape, not the shape. At 120px the specks vanish entirely and what survives is a hairline ring, which is jewellery, not a barrow.
findings.specificChange: Replace the stroke-only rendering of the primary members with solid filled polygons in charcoal/iron, and pin every child generation's centroid inside its parent's hull at no less than 40 percent of the parent's scale, so that the union of parent and children resolves to one continuous filled silhouette instead of a wire figure surrounded by debris. Reduce the child count to two or three per generation and cap generations at three.
findings.keep: Keep the single centred figure and the existing primitive families (ring, triangle, diamond, six-point star). This is a change to how members are filled and where children are placed, not a change to which shapes are chosen, and the outer contour of each seed must survive it recognisably.

findings.whatFails: The figure occupies roughly a quarter to a third of the frame's shorter dimension. In dev-single-512 the triangle spans about 130 of 512 pixels, sits left of centre and above centre, and is surrounded on all sides by a wide band of untouched near-black. Across the 12-seed sheet no token touches or crops at any frame edge.
findings.why: The composition direction asks for a mass that 'reaches well toward the frame edges and feels larger than the frame comfortably holds, with little clear space', and negativeSpace asks for the remainder to read as pressure. What is rendered is the exact opposite: a small emblem floating in a generous, comfortable, symmetric margin. Nothing is crowded, so nothing feels heavy or immovable.
findings.specificChange: Increase the root primitive's circumradius so the drawn silhouette's bounding box spans at least 90 percent of the shorter frame dimension, and deliberately let one or two members cross the viewBox edge so the mass is cropped rather than fully contained. Re-centre the root on the frame centre and cap the residual margin at roughly 5 percent per side.
findings.keep: Keep the crop deliberate and partial: the outer contour must still be readable as one closed silhouette at 120px, so do not enlarge until the figure exceeds the frame on all four sides and degenerates into an anonymous texture.

findings.whatFails: The ochre is not a seam anywhere in the sheet. It is the entire primary figure in all twelve seeds, and it is also the highest-contrast element in the image, while the charcoal/iron members are relegated to faint background ghosts at near-ground value. The value hierarchy is inverted relative to the brief.
findings.why: paletteIntent specifies 'charcoal and iron with a single ochre seam over near black, low contrast so the mass reads as weight'. Making the accent carry the whole form produces a bright emblem on black, which is high contrast and reads as light and decorative. Weight requires the mass to be the dark iron and the ochre to be a single localised interruption in it.
findings.specificChange: Recolour the dominant mass to filled charcoal/iron sitting only a little above the near-black ground, and reduce ochre to a single continuous seam along one member edge or one fracture line, targeting under roughly 8 percent of drawn area. Raise the iron members' value enough to separate them from the ground so the silhouette still reads once the ochre stops carrying it.
findings.keep: Keep the exact hue pair (warm ochre against cold charcoal over near-black) and keep the ochre as the single most saturated element in the frame, so that where the seam falls remains a per-seed variation axis as variationStrategy requires.

findings.whatFails: In dev-states-256 the stress row is a uniform scale-up with a heavier stroke, not a break. 5003 grows and its ring becomes an octagon; 5265's triangle simply gets bigger and bolder; 5396's rosette enlarges while its grey satellites drift. In every case the silhouette stays closed and continuous, no member separates from its neighbour, and recovery is close enough to neutral to be near-invisible.
findings.why: marketTransformation requires that 'the mass fractures and its members separate and the silhouette breaks', and thumbnailIntent requires the fracture to be visible at 120px as a broken outline. Scaling changes size, not structure, so the claimed change is not the claimed change. Worse, at browse size a bigger version of the same figure reads as a different token rather than as the same monument under stress.
findings.specificChange: Pin the root silhouette's overall scale constant across all three states, and drive stress instead by translating each member outward along its own centroid-to-parent vector by an offset that grows with drawdown, opening visible gaps in the outer contour so the silhouette becomes discontinuous. Let recovery close those gaps back toward zero offset rather than shrinking the figure.
findings.keep: Keep the state identity that is already working: the primitive family, the member count, the palette pairing and the centre position must stay fixed across neutral, stress and recovery, and recovery must continue to land close to neutral.

findings.whatFails: At 120px the twelve seeds collapse into about four families and clone inside them. 5134, 5658, 6051 and 6182 are all a plain ochre ring with faint grey debris and are effectively interchangeable; 5265, 5920 and 6444 are all the same right-pointing outlined triangle; 5003, 5396, 5527 and 6313 are all star-rosettes. Only 5789's diamond is unique. What varies between seeds is mostly the scatter of the grey satellites, which is invisible at browse size.
findings.why: variationStrategy says tokens differ 'first in the silhouette of the mass, then in its symmetry, then in where the ochre seam falls'. Here silhouette is a lottery over roughly four primitives and is identical within each family, so the primary variation axis carries almost no information and the secondary axes are carried by elements that do not survive downsampling. Twelve tokens read as four works repeated.
findings.specificChange: Widen the per-seed silhouette parameters so the outer contour differs between every pair of seeds: spread the member count across a wider range (for example 3 to 12 sides on the root), add a per-seed rotation offset and a per-seed asymmetric member displacement so no two tokens share the same outer contour, and move the ochre seam's position to a distinct per-seed index. Verify by regenerating the 120px sheet and requiring that no two tiles share a matching outline.
findings.keep: Keep the shared visual language: all tokens must stay one centred heavy mass built from a few large regular primitives in the same palette, so widening the silhouette range must not produce organic or irregular forms that break the geometric-recursion medium.

overall: This is not yet a barrow; it is a set of thin ochre emblems floating in comfortable black margins. The three things the brief is actually about -- mass, scale and fracture -- are all absent: nothing is filled, so there is no weight; the figure occupies about a quarter of the frame with an even margin on all sides, so there is no pressure and nothing feels larger than the frame can hold; and the stress state is a uniform zoom rather than a break, so the one transformation the brief names is not depicted. The palette is inverted on top of that, with the accent ochre carrying the entire form and the charcoal iron demoted to background dust, which makes every token read bright and decorative rather than dark and immovable. What is genuinely working and must be protected is the singular focal structure, the near-black ground, the correct hue pair, and the state identity: a token is unmistakably the same token across neutral, stress and recovery. The 120px sheet is where this fails hardest -- twelve seeds resolve into roughly four repeated families because silhouette, the brief's primary variation axis, is a small lottery over four primitives while all the real per-seed difference lives in grey satellites that disappear at browse size. The route forward is to fill the members, grow the root until it crops the frame, demote the ochre to a single seam, and make stress separate members instead of scaling them.
